claims.text: The precursor powders contain Group IV and refractory elements in hydride form, such as TiH2 and ZrH2.
The precursor powder has an initial oxygen content below 0.1 wt%.
Hydride precursors facilitate oxygen scavenging and hydrogen-assisted densification.
Hydrides should be decomposed immediately before and during extrusion under high vacuum below 10^-5 Pa or in argon.
Rapid heating to 800-1000 °C followed by a hold shorter than five minutes is sufficient for hydride decomposition while limiting oxygen ingress.
Extrusion should be performed at 1100-1300 °C, below the alloy solidus, and at high strain rate.
Maintaining oxygen partial pressure below 10^-6 atm prevents alpha-HCP nucleation.
Hydrogen released during hydride decomposition causes transient lattice expansion that assists pore closure during extrusion.
Rapid cooling in a low-oxygen environment stabilizes a metastable single-phase BCC solid solution.
Rapid cooling and low oxygen prevent segregation or precipitation of alpha-HCP, Laves, and B2 phases.
Hydride decomposition getters residual oxygen by producing volatile oxides or stable hydrides that can be evacuated.
A rapid thermal cycle suppresses the diffusion and nucleation kinetics required to form brittle alpha-HCP phases.
High-strain-rate extrusion refines the alloy grain size.
A fine-grained BCC matrix increases strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Elevated oxygen content can embrittle Group-IV-containing RHEAs and promote cracking during hot deformation.
Conventional processing with oxygen uptake above 0.5 wt% causes precipitation of brittle alpha-HCP phases.
The proposed process will produce a crack-free bulk RHEA with relative density above 98%.
The resulting bulk alloy will have a homogeneous BCC microstructure without brittle alpha-HCP precipitates.
The processed alloy will exhibit yield strength above 400 MPa at 1600 °C, comparable to or exceeding cast RHEAs.
The proposed process is specifically applicable to RHEAs containing more than 10 at% Group IV elements because such alloys are susceptible to alpha-HCP formation.
